newsitem.title: USA: Wall St stocks end choppy session lower.
newsitem.headline: Wall St stocks end choppy session lower.

text.p: U.S. blue chips whirled lower on Wednesday after a choppy session that saw sharp early gains unravel under pressure from a weakening U.S. dollar.
The Dow fell 33 points to close unofficially at 7928, the second straight losing session for blue chips. Broader indexes were mixed, with tech stocks scratching out modest gains.

Stocks started strongly, with the Dow initially spiking 80 points higher after reassuring reports on inflation and retail sales activity, only to track the bond market through a rapid reversal that sent blue chips to a similarly steep deficit.
Analysts pointed to currency markets in an attempt to explain the turnaround, noting that stocks seemed to have every reason to rally after the early data.
"This morning's numbers were nothing short of phenomenal from the market's perspective," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
"If you were to put a gun to my head and ask for one word that moved the markets today, it would be 'currency.'"
The dollar ended at 1.8345 German marks, down from 1.8630 marks at Tuesday's close. It also fell to 115.70 Japanese yen from 116.28.

While a weaker dollar over time can lift earnings at export- oriented U.S. companies, because of the beneficial effects on the translation of international sales, it also discourages institutions from holding dollar-based stocks and bonds.
After watching stocks fail to sustain their early gains, some analysts argued further nervous action may well lie ahead.

"I think the ingredients are there for an additional pullback," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "The volatility we saw today was a manifestation of the great deal of indecision that is in the market."

Leading the Dow lower were oil components Chevron Corp, down 1-13/16 to 79 and Exxon Corp, off 1-3/4 to 60-3/4. Analysts cited concern that Iraq's re-entry to oil markets would result in depressed prices for crude oil.
Among individual issues, chip maker Micron Technology Inc skidded 7-1/2 to 42-5/8 after several investment firms downgraded the shares over worries about memory pricing trends.
Micron was the New York Stock Exchange's most active issue, with more than 23 million shares changing hands in composite trading.

Central Sprinkler Corp fell 1/4 to 19-3/4 after media reports that a type of fire-sprinkler head produced by the company failed to work properly. Early in the session, the shares traded as low as 16-1/2.
CorporateFamily Solutions Inc jumped 3-5/8 to 13-5/8 in the company's Wall Street debut after launching its initial public offering. CorporateFamily provides child care at workplace sites.
Boeing Co rose 1-9/16 to 58-1/16. Smith Barney upgraded the shares today to strong buy based on expected cost savings from the company's merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp.
The S&P 500 index fell 4.51 points to 922.02.

The Nasdaq Composite rose 7.16 to 1583.40, lifted by a strong performance among semiconductor equipment makers. Applied Materials Inc sparked the rally, surging 9-1/8 to 99-3/9 after the company late Tuesday reported stronger than expected earnings.
